newsitem.title: USA: Wall Street shares seen opening slightly higher.
newsitem.headline: Wall Street shares seen opening slightly higher.

text.p: Wall Street is expected to open a bit higher on Tuesday, adding on to Friday's gains and boosted by activity in AT&T Corp, which is reported to be in merger talks with SBC Communications Corp.
Shares of telecommunications firms were seen supporting the Dow index, after the Wall Street Journal reported AT&T and SBC were discussing a merger deal valued at $50-billion plus.
"We should open today flat to slightly higher after the somewhat unexpected runup on Friday," Peter Carillo, director of research at Westfalia Investments said.

Telecommunications stocks were expected to be very active at the market open on heavy volume, analysts said. Shares of drug manufacturers would also draw attention after news of a large acquisition in Europe, they said.

Swiss pharmaceuticals group Roche Holding Ltd announced plans to buy diagnostics and pharmaceuticals company Boehringer Mannheim Group and a majority of orthopedics product company DePuy Inc in an $11 billion deal.
But other analysts cautioned that U.S. stock markets, which rose to record levels on Friday ahead of a holiday weekend, could lose ground at the open today.

"I think we will be soft at the open," Joseph Battipaglio, chief investment officer at Gruntal, said. "What we saw on Friday was a lot of portfolio manipulation, a short-term phenomenon. We could give back gains at the start."

On Friday, the Dow industrial average rose 88 points, or 1.2 percent, to close at 7346. On Tuesday, the Standard & Poor's futures index was up 0.05 points at 847.80, backing off slightly from levels hit earlier today.
The long bond was off 11/32 at a 7.02 percent yield, compared with Friday's yield of 6.99 percent.
Analysts have said stocks could weaken if the long bond hit a seven percent yield because money managers might shift funds from stocks into bonds and cash.
Among telecommunications stocks expected to be active this morning, analysts named GTE Corp, Bell Atlantic Corp and MCI Communications Corp.
Tokyo's 225-share Nikkei average fell 153.61 points, or 0.77 percent, to 19,889.89.
In London, the FTSE 100 was up 25.8 points at 4687.6. U.S. stocks held firm in London and dealers expected Wall Street to move further into record territory at the open.
The dollar was firm against the yen in Tokyo, trading at 116.20/30 yen after paring earlier losses. In Europe, the dollar was trading at 1.6986/91 marks.

The Wall Street Journal's Heard on the Street column reported that investors who are buying newly-issued shares and junk bonds are helping to bail Wall Street out of what could have been risky temporary loans.
The New York Times said its Market Place column said the market for new issues of high technology firms has fallen off. The recent slump seems to have been larger than analysts had expected.
